summary: Frontend-only verification of the mobile scroll performance CSS fix at mobile 375x700 and desktop 1920x800 across /, /login, /dashboard. Discovered ONE critical CSS-minification bug: the compiled production stylesheet is missing the standard `backdrop-filter: none !important;` declaration — only `-webkit-backdrop-filter:none!important` survived. All other fix goals (background-attachment: scroll on mobile / fixed on desktop, dark opaque surface fallbacks, halved decorative glow blurs, no horizontal overflow, login regression, hamburger drawer) verified working.

ui_bugs.issue: Inside the @media (max-width:1023px) block, the rule for `.surface-luxe, .clay-card, .clay-inset, .backdrop-blur-{sm,md,lg,xl,2xl,3xl}` compiled to ONLY `-webkit-backdrop-filter:none!important` — the standard unprefixed `backdrop-filter:none!important` was stripped by the CSS minifier (Lightning CSS de-duplicated the two identical declarations and kept only the -webkit one, since it appears last in source). Result: on modern Chromium/Firefox mobile the backdrop-filter still evaluates to `blur(24px)` / `blur(12px)` on every element that matched (verified via getComputedStyle on mobile 375px). This means the primary GPU-cost fix (kill live backdrop blurs while scrolling on mobile) is effectively a no-op on non-Safari mobile browsers. Visual appearance is unaffected because the opaque background-color fallback is still applied, but the scroll-lag issue the user reported is NOT actually mitigated.
ui_bugs.selector: .surface-luxe.backdrop-blur-xl (dashboard top-nav), .backdrop-blur-md (home hero badge), .backdrop-blur-xl (all pricing/feature cards on /)

action_items: In /app/app/globals.css MOBILE SCROLL PERFORMANCE block, swap the declaration order so the standard property comes LAST (put `-webkit-backdrop-filter: none !important;` first, then `backdrop-filter: none !important;`). This prevents the minifier from dropping the unprefixed one. Alternative fix: split into two separate rules, or add a decoy value diff (e.g. `filter: none !important;`) so the two declarations aren't seen as identical adjacent duplicates. Then run production build again.
After rebuild, re-verify on mobile 375px that computed `backdrop-filter` on `.surface-luxe`, `.clay-card`, and every `[class*="backdrop-blur"]` element equals `none`.
critical_code_review_comments: The current mobile performance CSS block relies on Tailwind utility class names (.backdrop-blur-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/3xl) — if any component uses arbitrary values like `backdrop-blur-[10px]`, this selector list will miss them. Consider adding `[class*='backdrop-blur-[']` as well.

Assertion writers should note: body has 3 stacked background layers, so getComputedStyle(body).backgroundAttachment returns a comma-joined value like 'scroll, scroll, scroll' or 'fixed, fixed, fixed'. Any test must parse the CSV, not string-compare against a single keyword.

rca of the issue: Reproduction: curl the served CSS chunk /_next/static/chunks/11f1c0d51bq~0.css and inspect the `@media (max-width:1023px)` block. Source globals.css has `backdrop-filter:none!important; -webkit-backdrop-filter:none!important;` but compiled output has only `-webkit-backdrop-filter:none!important`. Root cause: Next.js 16 uses Lightning CSS / SWC minifier which detects the two adjacent declarations with identical value on the same selector as duplicates and keeps the last one. Because `-webkit-backdrop-filter` appears second in source, it wins; the standard property is dropped. Modern mobile Chromium/Firefox read only the unprefixed `backdrop-filter`, so the override is invisible to them. Mitigation: reverse the declaration order in the source CSS (webkit first, standard last), OR use two separate rule blocks, OR break the value symmetry so the minifier can't dedupe.
